statement: In bash, `f || handler` disables `set -e` for everything inside `f`, so a failing command in `f` no longer stops it. Cejel's release driver called `currency_read "$id" || return 0` at stage 11 (the `||` was there for a dry-run in-flight return), and inside currency_read a failed `gh run view --log` therefore did not exit: the empty log went on to be counted, and the driver refused with 'reported 0 surfaces, expected 14', which named the wrong cause. The same read at stage 13, called without `||`, exited silently. Rules: never rely on `set -e` inside a function that any caller invokes with `||`, `&&`, `if` or `!`; check each failing command explicitly (`x=$(cmd) || die "..."`) and test the failure at every call site, since one function can fail differently depending on how it is called.
